inputs.research_brief: Türkiye'de yaşayan bir üniversite öğrencisiyim ve Kasım 2026'da derslerim ve yazılım geliştirme çalışmalarım için yeni bir dizüstü bilgisayar satın almak istiyorum. Türkiye'deki yetkili satıcılardan alınabilecek modelleri araştırın. KDV ve zorunlu teslimat ücretleri dahil toplam satın alma bedeli 45.000 TL'nin altında olmalı; tam 45.000 TL olan bir ürün bütçeme uygun değildir. En az 16 GB RAM, en az 512 GB SSD ve en fazla 1,6 kg ağırlık zorunlu koşullarım. Pil ömrünü ve fan gürültüsünü de karşılaştırın; sessiz çalışma tercih sebebi olsa da zorunlu değildir. İkinci el, yenilenmiş veya yalnızca ithalatçı garantisi bulunan ürünleri dahil etmeyin; Türkiye'de geçerli üretici garantisi istiyorum. Teknik özellikler için üreticilerin resmi belgelerine, fiyat ve stok bilgileri için yetkili satıcılara, gerçek kullanım performansı için bağımsız testlere öncelik verin. Fiyatları ve stok durumunu 9 Ekim 2026 itibarıyla kontrol edin, ancak Kasım ayındaki bulunabilirliği kesin kabul etmeyin. Uygun model bulunamaması ihtimalini de değerlendirin. Marka, ekran boyutu ve işletim sistemi konusunda bir kısıtım yok.

criteria: The plan investigates newly sold laptops available through authorized retailers in Turkey against a strict all-inclusive purchase price below TRY 45,000, including VAT and mandatory delivery charges; a price of exactly TRY 45,000 must not qualify.
The plan verifies that candidate laptops meet both mandatory hardware minimums of at least 16 GB RAM and at least 512 GB SSD storage.
The plan verifies laptop weight against the inclusive maximum of 1.6 kg, allowing models weighing exactly 1.6 kg.

The plan investigates retailer prices and stock information as of October 9, 2026, without assuming that currently listed laptops will remain available in November 2026, and allows for the possibility that no eligible model exists.
The plan compares battery endurance and fan noise across candidate laptops using a consistent evaluation basis, treating quiet operation as a preference rather than a mandatory eligibility condition.
The plan verifies manufacturer-backed warranty coverage valid in Turkey and excludes used, refurbished, and importer-warranty-only laptops.

The plan specifies collecting manufacturer documentation for technical specifications, authorized Turkish retailer evidence for prices and stock, and independent testing evidence for real-world performance.
The plan does not introduce unsupported restrictions on laptop brand, screen size, or operating system.

The plan organizes the laptop research into appropriately scoped, mostly independent investigative objectives with evidence-oriented success criteria, avoiding redundant objectives and standalone report-writing tasks.

inputs.research_brief: I manage a 25-person B2B sales organization in Ireland, and we need to select a CRM for deployment in the first quarter of 2027. Compare HubSpot Sales Hub, Pipedrive, and Zoho CRM on a consistent basis; Salesforce is outside the scope of this procurement. The CRM must support Microsoft 365 email synchronization and role-based user permissions. Our recurring subscription costs, including any add-ons required for those capabilities, must total at most EUR 2,000 per month for all 25 users, based on monthly billing rather than annual-payment discounts. Examine one-time migration expenses separately. We currently have approximately 100,000 contacts to import, so migration feasibility matters, as does ongoing administrative effort for a small internal IT team. EU-only data hosting is preferred because of our customers' expectations, but it is not mandatory, and options must not be rejected solely for lacking EU-only hosting. Base pricing and feature assessments on vendor information available as of October 9, 2026, and use technical documentation, contractual terms, or demonstrable product behavior to substantiate important claims. If deployment terms or prices for the first quarter of 2027 cannot be verified, identify that uncertainty rather than treating current offers as guaranteed. We have no preferred vendor or mandatory industry-specific sales workflow.

criteria: The plan compares HubSpot Sales Hub, Pipedrive, and Zoho CRM against a shared evaluation basis for an Irish B2B sales organization, without introducing Salesforce as an additional procurement candidate.

The plan investigates total recurring CRM subscription and necessary add-on costs for all 25 paid users against the inclusive EUR 2,000 monthly ceiling, using monthly billing rates rather than annual-payment discounts and assessing one-time migration expenses separately.
The plan verifies Microsoft 365 email synchronization support for each CRM candidate, including whether the capability depends on a particular subscription tier or add-on.
The plan verifies role-based user permission capabilities for each CRM candidate, including whether they are restricted to particular subscription tiers.
The plan investigates the feasibility, limitations, and potential expenses of migrating approximately 100,000 existing contacts into each CRM candidate.
The plan compares the ongoing administrative effort required to operate HubSpot Sales Hub, Pipedrive, and Zoho CRM with a small internal IT team.
The plan investigates EU-only data hosting as a preference for the CRM procurement, without treating its absence as grounds for automatically excluding a candidate.

The plan specifies verification of CRM capabilities, current pricing, and contractual conditions through relevant vendor technical evidence available as of October 9, 2026, while recognizing that first-quarter 2027 deployment terms and prices may remain uncertain.

The plan uses distinct, appropriately scoped investigative tasks with meaningful evidence requirements in their success criteria, rather than duplicative research objectives or standalone final-report tasks.

inputs.research_brief: I am preparing an evidence review for a pediatric sleep clinic deciding whether to offer digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia, or digital CBT-I, to adolescents aged 12–17 with clinically identified insomnia. I want to understand whether digital CBT-I improves sleep onset latency and daytime functioning compared with usual care, and what the evidence says about treatment adherence and reported adverse effects. Restrict eligible evidence to original randomized controlled trials published in peer-reviewed English-language journals between January 1, 2018 and September 30, 2026, inclusive. Do not include systematic reviews, narrative reviews, adult-only studies, medication interventions, or studies whose participants were not identified as having insomnia. Examine the methodological quality and risk of bias of eligible studies, investigate disagreements in findings, and distinguish unsupported conclusions from evidence of no benefit. If the available trials do not address an outcome adequately, that limitation matters to the decision. I have not selected a particular digital CBT-I product, and I do not want the research restricted to one application or delivery platform.

criteria: The plan restricts eligible clinical effectiveness evidence for adolescent digital CBT-I to original randomized controlled trials and explicitly excludes systematic reviews and other secondary reviews.
The plan applies an inclusive publication window of January 1, 2018 through September 30, 2026, to peer-reviewed English-language evidence concerning digital CBT-I.
The plan investigates evidence specific to adolescents aged 12–17 with clinically identified insomnia, excluding adult-only populations and studies without an identified insomnia population.
The plan investigates digital cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia compared with usual care, without substituting medication-based insomnia interventions.
The plan investigates the effect of digital CBT-I on sleep onset latency in adolescents with insomnia, specifying collection of comparative outcome evidence rather than assuming a benefit.
The plan investigates the effect of digital CBT-I on daytime functioning in adolescents with insomnia as an outcome distinct from sleep onset latency.
The plan investigates both treatment adherence and reported adverse effects associated with digital CBT-I in the eligible adolescent population.
The plan specifies appraisal of methodological quality, risk of bias, disagreements between eligible studies, and evidence gaps without treating absent evidence as proof of no benefit.

The plan structures the clinical evidence review around separable investigative objectives with meaningful evidence-oriented success criteria, avoiding redundant tasks and standalone report-writing objectives.

inputs.research_brief: 14–16 Mayıs 2027 tarihlerinde bir yakınımla Ankara'dan İstanbul'a seyahat etmeyi planlıyorum. İkimiz de yetişkiniz; ben 75 kg ağırlığında akülü tekerlekli sandalye kullanıyorum ve sandalyemin genişliği 68 cm. Ankara Kızılay'dan İstanbul Kadıköy'e gidiş ve dönüş için yüksek hızlı tren ile uçak seçeneklerini kapıdan kapıya karşılaştırmak istiyorum. 14 Mayıs'ta Kadıköy'e en geç saat 15.00'te ulaşmalıyız ve 16 Mayıs'ta İstanbul'dan saat 17.00'den önce ayrılmak istemiyoruz. İki kişinin gidiş-dönüş biletleri ve zorunlu şehir içi transferleri dahil toplam bütçemiz en fazla 18.000 TL. Araca erişim, peron veya terminal altyapısı, sandalyenin taşınma koşulları ve erişilebilir transfer seçenekleri benim için belirleyici. Sandalyemin akü tipi ve kapasitesi henüz net değil; özellikle hava yolu kurallarına uygunluğunu doğrulamadan varsaymayın. Özel araçla yolculuk istemiyoruz. Resmi TCDD, hava yolu şirketi, havalimanı ve ulaşım işletmecisi kaynaklarına öncelik verin. Mayıs 2027 seferlerinin, fiyatlarının veya erişilebilir hizmetlerinin henüz ilan edilmemiş olabileceğini hesaba katın; doğrulanamayan uygunluğu veya rezervasyon bulunabilirliğini kesin bilgi gibi sunmayın.

criteria: The plan compares high-speed rail and air travel as end-to-end round-trip transportation alternatives between Kızılay in Ankara and Kadıköy in Istanbul, including necessary ground transfers rather than only station-to-station or airport-to-airport travel.
The plan investigates schedules and travel-time feasibility for arrival in Kadıköy no later than 15:00 on May 14, 2027, and departure from Istanbul no earlier than 17:00 on May 16, 2027.
The plan verifies boarding, vehicle accommodation, station or terminal access, and transfer accessibility for a powered wheelchair weighing 75 kg and measuring 68 cm in width.

The plan investigates airline battery-transport requirements for a powered wheelchair and explicitly treats the currently unspecified battery chemistry and capacity as unresolved information requiring verification.
The plan investigates the combined cost of round-trip transportation tickets for two adults and mandatory local transfers against an inclusive total ceiling of TRY 18,000.

The plan seeks verification of May 14–16, 2027 service schedules, fares, accessible arrangements, and reservation availability, recognizing that future information may not yet be published or bookable.
The plan prioritizes applicable official evidence from TCDD, airlines, airports, and transport operators when investigating accessibility procedures and operating conditions.
The plan excludes private-car travel from the Ankara–Istanbul comparison without prematurely ruling out either rail or air alternatives before accessibility and feasibility have been investigated.
The plan decomposes the travel research into distinct actionable investigations with meaningful evidence requirements, avoiding redundant tasks or standalone itinerary-writing objectives.

inputs.research_brief: Ankara'dan İzmir'e taşınacağım ve 1 Aralık 2026'da başlayacak 12 aylık bir kira sözleşmesi için ev arıyorum. Bornova ile Karşıyaka'yı karşılaştırmak istiyorum; şimdilik başka ilçeleri araştırmaya gerek yok. Ege Üniversitesi Bornova kampüsünde çalışacağım. Hafta içi sabah 08.30'da işte olabilmek için toplu taşımayla kapıdan kapıya yolculuk süresi en fazla 45 dakika olmalı. Aidat dahil aylık toplam konut giderim 38.000 TL'yi aşamaz. En az iki yatak odası olmalı ve kedimle yaşamama açıkça izin verilmesi zorunlu. Bina yaşı, deprem yönetmeliğiyle ilgili belgeler ve erişilebilen güvenlik verilerini değerlendirmek istiyorum; ancak belgelerden kesin deprem dayanıklılığı sonucu çıkarılmasını istemiyorum. Öncelikle gerçek ilanlara, emlakçı veya ev sahibi doğrulamalarına ve belediye ya da diğer resmi kaynaklara dayanın. 9–25 Ekim 2026 tarihleri arasında erişilebilen ilanları kontrol edin; Aralık ayındaki kiralanabilirliği doğrulanmadan varsaymayın. Kısa dönem tatil kiralamalarını dahil etmeyin. Kat, manzara veya mobilya konusunda zorunlu tercihim bulunmuyor.

criteria: The plan compares long-term rental housing opportunities in Bornova and Karşıyaka in Izmir using a consistent evaluation basis, without expanding the geographic search to unrelated districts.
The plan checks the combined monthly rent and building maintenance dues for candidate properties against an inclusive TRY 38,000 monthly housing-cost ceiling.
The plan investigates rental eligibility for a 12-month lease beginning December 1, 2026, while excluding short-term holiday rentals.
The plan verifies that rental properties provide at least two bedrooms rather than treating a two-room apartment as automatically sufficient.
The plan investigates whether each candidate rental explicitly permits the tenant to live with a cat, treating permission as mandatory rather than a preference.
The plan evaluates weekday public-transport journeys from candidate homes to the Ege University Bornova campus against a maximum door-to-door commute of 45 minutes for arrival by 08:30.

The plan investigates building age, relevant earthquake-code documentation, and available official safety information for candidate housing, while avoiding unsupported claims of definitive earthquake resistance.

The plan specifies checking listings accessible during October 9–25, 2026, using property listings, agents or landlords, and relevant official sources to verify information, without assuming availability for December 1, 2026.

The plan divides rental research into mostly independent, evidence-oriented investigative objectives with meaningful success criteria and minimal unnecessary overlap, rather than separate report-production tasks.

inputs.research_brief: I lead the backend platform team for an analytics product running entirely on AWS. We need to choose an event-streaming architecture for a production deployment in the AWS Europe (Frankfurt) region by March 2027. Compare self-managed Apache Kafka on AWS infrastructure, Confluent Cloud, and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Our peak ingestion workload is 8,000 events per second with an average event size of 2 KB. Events must remain available for replay for at least 30 days, and the downstream analytics system should be able to query newly ingested information within five minutes of ingestion. All event data must remain in the Frankfurt region. The recurring infrastructure and managed-service budget is at most EUR 12,000 per month; our internal engineering labor is assessed separately rather than counted toward that limit. At-least-once delivery is acceptable, provided duplicate-processing implications and recovery after consumer failures are investigated. Do not turn exactly-once delivery into a mandatory requirement. We have two engineers available for routine platform operations and on-call work, so operational burden is a significant concern. Use vendor technical documentation and published pricing to establish capabilities and cost assumptions, checking the relevance of available performance benchmarks rather than applying them uncritically. If implementation feasibility depends on unspecified workload characteristics such as partition-key distribution or consumer processing complexity, investigate those dependencies rather than silently choosing favorable assumptions. I have no preferred provider among the three alternatives.

criteria: The plan compares self-managed Apache Kafka on AWS, Confluent Cloud, and Amazon Kinesis Data Streams on a shared technical and operational basis for a production analytics workload hosted on AWS.

The plan investigates ingestion capacity and scaling requirements for a peak workload of 8,000 events per second with an average payload of 2 KB, accounting for material uncertainties such as partition-key distribution.

The plan investigates whether each architecture can support downstream queryability of newly ingested analytics data within five minutes of ingestion, including relevant processing dependencies rather than considering ingestion throughput alone.
The plan investigates replay and retention capabilities for at least 30 days of event data across the three streaming alternatives.
The plan treats confinement of all event data to the AWS Europe (Frankfurt) region as a mandatory architecture constraint and verifies relevant deployment and data-residency capabilities.

The plan estimates recurring infrastructure and managed-service costs for the specified streaming workload against the inclusive EUR 12,000 monthly ceiling, while evaluating internal engineering labor separately.
The plan investigates at-least-once delivery, duplicate-processing implications, and recovery after consumer failures without imposing exactly-once delivery as a mandatory eligibility condition.

The plan compares the operational and on-call workload of the streaming alternatives against the capacity of a two-engineer operations team, using relevant vendor documentation, pricing, and appropriately qualified benchmark evidence.

The plan separates performance, reliability, cost, and operational feasibility into actionable and minimally overlapping investigative objectives with evidence-based success criteria, without adding standalone final-report tasks.

inputs.research_brief: I am a transport policy analyst advising a city council in England on whether to introduce a zero-fare local bus program for residents under 18. Before making a funding decision, I need an evidence review of comparable youth fare-free bus policies and evaluations from England and Scotland. I am interested in changes in bus ridership, access to education and other essential activities, and the financial implications for public authorities and bus operators. The research should distinguish genuine zero-fare eligibility for under-18 passengers from discounted or capped fares that still require payment; adult-only free-fare schemes are outside the scope. Focus on evidence describing outcomes observed between January 1, 2019 and December 31, 2025, while considering publications dated January 1, 2020 through September 30, 2026. These observation and publication windows are separate requirements. Compare urban and rural contexts where relevant, since local service frequency and baseline transport access may influence results. Prioritize official transport statistics, government or local-authority evaluations, and peer-reviewed studies, but examine methodological weaknesses rather than accepting every reported policy effect as causal. Where results conflict, investigate whether differences in policy eligibility, local conditions, measurement, or research design could explain them. I have not specified a subsidy budget, target ridership increase, or exact implementation model, so do not impose arbitrary thresholds. The goal is to assess evidence useful for the funding decision, not to assume that free fares necessarily produce benefits.

criteria: The plan investigates evidence concerning genuinely zero-fare local bus eligibility for passengers under 18, excluding adult-only schemes and policies that merely discount or cap fares while requiring payment.
The plan compares relevant youth fare-free bus policy evidence from England and Scotland using common outcome definitions or an explicitly comparable evaluation basis.

The plan distinguishes the eligible outcome-observation period of January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2025, from the eligible publication window of January 1, 2020 through September 30, 2026, rather than treating them as the same date constraint.

The plan investigates changes in bus ridership associated with youth zero-fare policies, seeking outcome measurements and relevant baseline or comparison information rather than assuming ridership increased.
The plan investigates whether youth zero-fare bus policies affect access to education and other essential activities, distinguishing access-related outcomes from ridership counts alone.

The plan investigates financial implications of youth zero-fare bus policies for both public authorities and bus operators, including the evidence needed to assess subsidy or reimbursement consequences without inventing a fixed budget.
The plan examines how urban versus rural conditions, service frequency, and baseline transport access may affect the applicability or interpretation of youth zero-fare bus policy evidence.

The plan prioritizes official transport statistics, government or local-authority evaluations, and peer-reviewed studies while investigating causal identification limitations, conflicting results, and potential explanations involving eligibility differences, local conditions, measurements, or study design.

The plan uses distinct, appropriately scoped investigative objectives with meaningful evidence requirements in task success criteria, avoiding redundant tasks, arbitrary success thresholds, and standalone report-writing objectives.
